analysis: In evaluating a CT scan for cranioencephalic trauma, it is crucial to identify the specific characteristics of different types of hemorrhages. An acute subdural hematoma typically appears as a crescent-shaped hyperdensity on a CT scan and can cross suture lines. An epidural hematoma, on the other hand, presents as a biconvex (lens-shaped) hyperdensity that does not cross suture lines. A cortical injury or cerebral contusion is characterized by patchy hyperdensities adjacent to the skull. Intraventricular hemorrhage is identified by hyperdensity within the ventricles.
